+import pytest
+
+import sqlparse
+from sqlparse import sql, tokens as T
+
+
+def walk(node):
+    yield node
+    for child in node.get_sublists():
+        yield from walk(child)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('spacing', [' ', '   ', '\t', '\n', '\r\n', ' \t\n '])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('clause,boundary,tail', [
+    ('WHERE', 'ORDER BY', 'x'),
+    ('WHERE', 'GROUP BY', 'x'),
+    ('WHERE', 'UNION ALL', 'SELECT y FROM u'),
+    ('QUALIFY', 'ORDER BY', 'x'),
+    ('QUALIFY', 'UNION ALL', 'SELECT y FROM u'),
+])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('nested', [False, True])
+def test_compound_boundaries(spacing, clause, boundary, tail, nested):
+    spelling = spacing.join(boundary.lower().split())
+    prefix = clause.lower() + ' x > 0 \t'
+    inner = 'SELECT x FROM t ' + prefix + spelling + ' ' + tail
+    source = 'SELECT * FROM (' + inner + ') AS q' if nested else inner
+    stmt, = sqlparse.parse(source)
+    container = next(n for n in walk(stmt) if isinstance(n, sql.Parenthesis)) if nested else stmt
+    cls = sql.Where if clause == 'WHERE' else sql.Qualify
+    groups = [t for t in container.tokens if isinstance(t, cls)]
+    assert len(groups) == 1
+    group = groups[0]
+    assert str(group) == prefix
+    index = container.token_index(group)
+    terminator = container.tokens[index + 1]
+    assert terminator.ttype is T.Keyword
+    assert terminator.value == spelling
+    assert terminator.normalized == spelling.upper()
+    assert str(stmt) == source
+    assert stmt.get_type() == 'SELECT'
+    for node in walk(stmt):
+        for child in node.tokens:
+            assert child.parent is node
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('nested', [False, True])
+def test_where_then_qualify(nested):
+    inner = 'SELECT x FROM t WHERE x > 0 QUALIFY n = 1 OrDeR\tBy x'
+    source = '(' + inner + ')' if nested else inner
+    stmt, = sqlparse.parse(source)
+    container = next(n for n in walk(stmt) if isinstance(n, sql.Parenthesis)) if nested else stmt
+    where = [t for t in container.tokens if isinstance(t, sql.Where)]
+    qualify = [t for t in container.tokens if isinstance(t, sql.Qualify)]
+    assert len(where) == len(qualify) == 1
+    assert str(where[0]) == 'WHERE x > 0 '
+    assert str(qualify[0]) == 'QUALIFY n = 1 '
+    assert container.tokens[container.token_index(qualify[0]) + 1].value == 'OrDeR\tBy'
+    assert str(stmt) == source
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('clause,terminator,tail', [
+    ('WHERE', 'LIMIT', '2'),
+    ('WHERE', 'HAVING', 'x > 1'),
+    ('WHERE', 'RETURNING', 'x'),
+    ('WHERE', 'INTO', 'u'),
+    ('QUALIFY', 'LIMIT', '2'),
+    ('QUALIFY', 'UNION', 'SELECT y FROM u'),
+    ('QUALIFY', 'EXCEPT', 'SELECT y FROM u'),
+    ('QUALIFY', 'INTERSECT', 'SELECT y FROM u'),
+])
+def test_single_word_boundaries(clause, terminator, tail):
+    source = 'SELECT x FROM t ' + clause + ' x > 0 ' + terminator + ' ' + tail
+    stmt, = sqlparse.parse(source)
+    cls = sql.Where if clause == 'WHERE' else sql.Qualify
+    group, = [t for t in stmt.tokens if isinstance(t, cls)]
+    assert str(group) == clause + ' x > 0 '
+    assert stmt.tokens[stmt.token_index(group) + 1].value == terminator
+    assert str(stmt) == source
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('clause', ['WHERE', 'QUALIFY'])
+def test_no_boundary_and_quoted_boundary(clause):
+    body = clause + " x = 'ORDER\tBY' AND y = 'UNION\nALL' "
+    source = '(SELECT x FROM t ' + body + ')'
+    stmt, = sqlparse.parse(source)
+    container = next(n for n in walk(stmt) if isinstance(n, sql.Parenthesis))
+    cls = sql.Where if clause == 'WHERE' else sql.Qualify
+    group, = [t for t in container.tokens if isinstance(t, cls)]
+    assert str(group) == body
+    assert container.tokens[-1].match(T.Punctuation, ')')
+    assert str(stmt) == source
+
+
+def test_token_matching_remains_exact():
+    token = sql.Token(T.Keyword, 'oRdEr\tbY')
+    assert token.value == 'oRdEr\tbY'
+    assert token.normalized == 'ORDER\tBY'
+    assert not token.match(T.Keyword, 'ORDER BY')
+    assert token.match(T.Keyword, 'ORDER\tBY')
+    assert not sql.Token(T.Name, 'ORDER\tBY').match(T.Keyword, 'ORDER\tBY')
+
+
+def test_qualify_keeps_non_boundary_compounds():
+    source = 'SELECT x FROM t QUALIFY n = 1 GROUP\tBY x'
+    stmt, = sqlparse.parse(source)
+    group, = [t for t in stmt.tokens if isinstance(t, sql.Qualify)]
+    assert str(group) == 'QUALIFY n = 1 GROUP\tBY x'

spec.question:
Make parsed WHERE and QUALIFY clauses terminate correctly when compound boundary keywords contain tabs, newlines, or multiple spaces between their words. For example, in `SELECT x FROM t WHERE x > 0 QUALIFY n = 1 ORDER\tBY x`, where `\t` denotes a literal tab, ORDER BY must remain outside the QUALIFY group. UNION ALL with a newline between its words must likewise remain outside the preceding clause.

This snapshot does not yet expose QUALIFY as a clause group, so include a public `sqlparse.sql.Qualify` TokenList subclass and its grouping integration. WHERE must end before ORDER BY, GROUP BY, LIMIT, UNION, UNION ALL, EXCEPT, INTERSECT, HAVING, RETURNING, INTO, or QUALIFY. QUALIFY must end before ORDER BY, LIMIT, UNION, UNION ALL, EXCEPT, or INTERSECT. Boundary recognition must be case-insensitive and insensitive to the whitespace separating words within a compound keyword token recognized by the lexer. Only keyword tokens at the clause's own nesting level count as boundaries; quoted text must not terminate a clause.

Both clause groups must work at statement level and inside parentheses. Include whitespace preceding a boundary in the clause, but exclude the boundary itself. With no boundary, include the remaining groupable tokens without consuming enclosing parenthesis delimiters. Preserve exact token values, SQL round-tripping, statement-type detection, and parent relationships. Do not change the global semantics of `Token.normalized` or `Token.match`, or broaden the boundary handling of unrelated groups. Return a unified diff changing production files only.
